newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France delays France Telecom sale for poll.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France delays France Telecom sale for poll.

text.p: France on Tuesday postponed the country's biggest privatisation project, the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom because it conflicts with the election called by President Jacques Chirac.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a statement he had decided to delay the sale of France Telecom shares by four weeks because of the parliamentary polls.
The ministry said the election will not affect the timetable for the private sale of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF expected later in the year.
The first round of the election will be on May 25, which would have been the eve of the announcement of the France Telecom sale price. The second round of the poll is on June 1.
Under the new timetable, private French investors will be allowed to reserve shares beginning around June 5. The international Initial Public Offer (IPO) will run from June 24 to July 1.

"It's a wise decision," said a London-based telecommunications sector analyst. "For institutional investors it removes the bit of political uncertainty that could have weighed on the sale if it had gone ahead as planned," he added.
"For the French private investors, who are going to be a key driver in this sale, it will mean that they can give full attention to the sale after the elections are over," he said.
The June sale takes place before the French school holidays in July and August, and the four-week delay does not upset the international timetable of privatisations, he added.

The sale of a 30 percent stake in France Telecom, estimated at between 160 billion and 210 billion francs ($36 billion), could become the biggest French market operation ever and could make France Telecom the company with the biggest market capitalisation in France ahead of oil-group Elf-Aquitaine.
France Telecom, ranked fourth globally in sales terms, would also rank in the top 10 in market value when it is sold at an expected price range of between 170 and 180 francs per share.
Arthuis said in his statement that the sale needed an important public relations campaign which was difficult to conduct during an election campaign.
He said the decision confirmed the government's desire to conclude rapidly France Telecom's partial privatisation ahead of full liberalisation in the European telecommunications sector in 1998.
Analysts said that the final France Telecom sale price would now depend on the trends in the French stock market.
"If the government gets re-elected with a smaller majority, the market will be stable. If he wins convincingly, the market could even rally," an analyst said.

"It all depends on the French share market. If the market falls 10 percent due to the political situation, they will have to look at the valuation again but if the market stays flat it could still go ahead as planned," said analyst Robert Mocatta at BZW in London.
The opposition Socialist party said in November it wanted France Telecom to remain a state company.
A spokesman at France Telecom said the company "took note" of the decision to delay the sale by four weeks and added that nothing else had changed.
The government has allowed both Lagardere Groupe and a team of Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industrie to refine their bids and make final offers before May 7.
